findings.title: Custom user installation path permits persistent shell command injection
findings.what: For `--user` with a custom directory, HOOK_PATH contains the caller-controlled absolute path. Validation rejects only double quotes and backslashes, then line 73 embeds the path inside a shell command stored in settings.json. A legal directory component such as `$(touch marker)` or a backtick substitution remains active inside the generated double-quoted shell word and executes whenever Stop or SessionEnd evaluates the registration, potentially with CLAUDE_HUB_TOKEN present.
findings.fix: Generate the registered command using robust shell argument quoting (for example, quote the literal custom path with `printf %q` while handling the intentional `$HOME` form structurally), and reject control characters; do not interpolate an untrusted path directly into shell source.
findings.acceptance: Install with `--user` into a temporary absolute directory whose literal name contains `$(touch <marker>)`, invoke the generated registration in an isolated environment, and assert that the marker is not created and the literal installed hook path is used. Repeat with a backtick-containing directory and verify settings.json remains valid JSON.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read tools/cloud-capture/install.sh:41-73. Lines 44-55 preserve shell metacharacters from the custom path; lines 66-71 exclude only `"` and `\`; line 73 places the remaining value in executable double-quoted shell source. Inside double quotes, both `$()` and backticks still perform command substitution, so the claim is directly reproducible and is not mitigated by later JSON escaping.
